AirAbsorption.description:
Air absorption: `condition_atmospherique@disable_absatmo_computation` and `@absatmo`.

In JSON: `{"kind": "iso9613"}` or `{"kind": "user_defined", "value": v, "unit": u}`. Extra
keys are refused for both kinds, so a hand-edited `{"kind": "iso9613", "value": 0.5}` is an
error, not a silent switch to the computed value.

oneOf.description: Computed by the solver per band from temperature, humidity and pressure (ISO 9613-1).
One value for every band, with its unit.

value.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

AttenuationUnit.description: Unit of a user-defined air absorption.

oneOf.description:
Energy attenuation per metre (1/m): energy falls as `exp(-m x)`. This is what the solver
reads from `@absatmo`, verbatim.

Level attenuation in dB per metre. The solver's own computed path converts dB/m by
ln(10)/10 (`base_core_configuration.cpp:111-115`); so does
[`AttenuationUnit::to_per_metre`].

BandData.description:
Every per-band array of a project, keyed by entity in project order: what changes with the
band set. Custom spectrum shapes are `Some`, other shapes `None`.

BandSet.description:
The frequency bands every per-band value in the project is given on.

`frequencies_hz` holds nominal centre frequencies of `kind`, strictly ascending. The solvers
sort `freq_enum` and map every per-band array by sorted position, so ascending order here is
the order of every per-band array in the project.

Diffusion law inside a fitting zone: `encombrement/bfreq@loi_diff`, the solver's
`DIFFUSION_LAW` (`lib_interface/coreTypes.h:108-113`). The discriminant is the solver code.

Directivity.description:
Source directivity: `source@directivite`, the solver's `SOURCE_TYPE`
(`lib_interface/coreTypes.h:96-104`). See [`Directivity::solver_code`].

In JSON: `{"kind": "omni"}`, `{"kind": "unidirectional", "direction": [x, y, z]}`, ...
Extra keys are refused for every kind. (serde's derive alone would read
`{"kind": "omni", "file": "balloon.txt"}` as omni and drop the file, so the reader is written
by hand.)

Code 1: emits along `direction` (`@u`, `@v`, `@w`, normalised by the solver).

The medium: `condition_atmospherique`. A missing element would leave the sound speed and
density at 0, so config.xml always writes every attribute.

FittingShape.description:
The volume of a fitting zone. Export marks it as a TetGen region whose attribute is the zone's
solver id (`mbin idVolume`, `.cbin idEn`).

oneOf.description:
An axis-aligned box, upstream's rectangular fitting zone (element type 56,
`e_scene_encombrements_encombrement_cuboide.h`). `min` and `max` are its bounds, for every
geometric use.

destination.description:
Which bound upstream's destination corner `hc` ("Destination volume") takes on each
axis; its origin corner `ba` takes the other. Upstream stores the two corners as the
user typed them, not ordered (tutorial 3's box: `ba` (13, 4, 0), `hc` (18, 1, 1.2)),
and seeds the box's TetGen region at `hc - (hc - ba) * 1e-4`
(`e_scene_encombrements_encombrement_cuboide.h:333-336`), so this is what reproduces
that seed ([`FittingShape::box_corners`]). `None`: `ba` is `min` and `hc` is `max`,
as for a box drawn here.

file in any other unit is refused rather than misread.

reflection_law.description: `bfreq@loi`, one law for every band or one per band.

scattering.description:
Scattering coefficient per band, 0 to 1: the share of reflections that are diffuse
(`bfreq@diffusion`).

solver_id.description:
A pinned solver id (`type_surface@id`, the `.cbin` face `idMat`). `None` lets export
assign one. Importers set it so that a project imported from a solver mesh exports the
same ids and still matches that mesh. At most [`SOLVER_INT_MAX`]: the solver reads
`@id` with `atoi`.

transmission_loss_db.description:
Transmission loss per band in dB (`bfreq@affaiblissement`, tau = 10^(-R/10)). `None`
means no transmission in any band; a `None` band does not transmit. Either way the
attribute is left out of that band, which is how the solver knows
(`base_core_configuration.cpp:210-219`), as upstream's GUI leaves it out of a band whose
`transmission` switch is off (`e_data_row_materiau.h:98-106`): tutorial 3's
`Open_door` transmits from 250 Hz to 4 kHz but not at 125 Hz.

anyOf.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

reflection_law.description: One law, which fits any band set, or one per band.

MaterialQuantity.description: A per-band quantity of a material.

max_volume_m3.description: `-a`: maximum tetrahedron volume, cubic metres; `None` for no bound.

preprocess.description:
Upstream's "Scene correction before meshing" (`mesh_conf@preprocess`,
`e_core_core_tetconf.h:108`): the `.poly` goes through upstream's `preprocess.exe` before
TetGen, with box fitting zones in its user facet list, as upstream's GUI does it
(`projet_maillage.cpp:206-213`). The geometry check then runs on what `preprocess.exe`
wrote. Upstream's GUI default is on; this crate's default is off
(`docs/m5-m6-design.md`, decision 12).

preserve_boundary.description: `-Y`: add no Steiner points on the boundary.

anyOf.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

surface_receiver_max_area_m2.description:
Facet-area constraint on surface-receiver faces, square metres (the `.var` file); `None`
for no refinement.

Op.description:
One edit. [`Op::apply`] returns its exact inverse.

`Add*` ops insert at `index` (at most the list length); their inverse is `Remove*` by id,
whose inverse re-inserts at the same index. `Replace*` ops swap a whole entity, found by its
id. A removal is refused while anything refers to the entity.

oneOf.description: Changes the band set and every per-band array at once; see [`Project::rebanded`].
Replaces the whole mesh (a re-import). Every face's group must exist.

Applies `ops` in order, all or nothing. The inverse is the inverses in reverse order.

background_noise.description: Background noise, `bfreq@db` per band. `None` writes none.

Project.description:
A room-acoustics project: the model, its materials, sources and receivers, the solver settings
and the GUI state.

active_variant.description: The variant the GUI shows and a run uses; `None` is the base project.

bands.description: The one band set every per-band array follows (`freq_enum`).

materials.description: The project's material library. Entries need not be in use.

ReflectionLaw.description:
How a surface reflects the diffuse part of the energy: `type_surface/bfreq@loi`, the solver's
`REFLECTION_LAW` (`lib_interface/coreTypes.h:83-92`). The discriminant is the solver code.

SPPS draws a diffuse reflection with probability equal to the scattering coefficient
(`spps/CalculationCore.cpp:318`), so the law has no effect at scattering 0.
[`ReflectionLaw::SemiDiffuse`] has no case in SPPS's `ReflectionLaws::SolveReflection`
(`spps/tools/dotreflection.h:23-45`) and falls to its default, a specular reflection.

oneOf.description: Uniform, `w1` in upstream's comments.

anyOf.description: The same law in every band.
One law per band; its length is the band count (`Project::check_integrity`).

ReflectionLaws.description:
A material's reflection law: one law for every band, or one per band. The solvers read it per
band (`type_surface/bfreq@loi`, `base_core_configuration.cpp:210-219`), and upstream's GUI
keeps one per band (the `loi` list of each row, `e_data_row_materiau.h:218`): tutorial 3's
material 100 is Lambert in the six octave bands and specular in the others.

In JSON: one law, `"lambert"`, or one per band in the band set's order,
`["specular", "lambert", ...]`. [`ReflectionLaws::from_bands`] gives the single spelling
whenever every band has the same law.

SolverSettings.description: Settings of every solver the project can run.

SoundMapQuantity.description: What SPPS writes on surface receivers: `simulation@surf_receiv_method`.

oneOf.description: Code 0: angle-weighted intensity.
Code 1: sound pressure level.

enabled.description: A disabled source is left out of config.xml.

position.description:
`@x`, `@y`, `@z`. Must lie strictly inside the meshed volume: SPPS crashes on a source
outside it (contract survey, `run_srcout`).

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

power.description: Sound power, dB re 1 pW (`bfreq@db` per band, from [`Spectrum::band_levels_db`]).

Spectrum.description:
A level spectrum: a global level spread over the project's bands by a shape.

Used for source sound power (dB re 1 pW) and receiver background noise.

global_db.description: The energetic sum over the project's bands, in dB.

SpectrumShape.description:
The shape of a level spectrum across the project's bands.

In JSON: `{"kind": "pink"}`, `{"kind": "white"}` or `{"kind": "custom", "relative_db": [...]}`.
Extra keys are refused for every kind: serde's derive alone would read
`{"kind": "pink", "relative_db": [...]}` as pink and drop the levels, so the reader is written
by hand.

oneOf.description: Equal power in every band.

Power proportional to bandwidth: +1 dB per third-octave band and +3 dB per octave band,
exactly (base-10 bands). This is I-Simpa's "White noise": tutorial 1's source, 80 dB
over 50 Hz to 20 kHz in thirds, reads 60.1404190063477 dB at 1 kHz, and this shape gives
60.14042 dB.
Relative levels in dB, one per band. Only the differences matter.

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

SppsSettings.description:
SPPS, the particle solver: the `simulation` element's SPPS attributes.

The three integers are C `int`s in the solver: each is at most [`SOLVER_INT_MAX`], which
[`Project::check_integrity`] enforces.

bands_computed.description: `freq_enum/bfreq@docalc` per band: which bands SPPS computes.

direct_field_only.description: `@direct_calc`: direct field only (every surface fully absorbing).

echogram_per_source.description: `@output_recp_bysource`: an echogram per source as well as the total.

extinction_exponent.description:
`@trans_epsilon`: a particle dies below `E0 * 10^-n`. A missing value (0) kills every
particle at the first step in energetic mode (contract survey, `run_noeps`).

fittings.description: `@enc_calc`: fitting zones on. Off, the solver ignores them silently.

particles_per_source.description: `@nbparticules`: particles per source per band. The solver raises values below 1 to 1.

particles_saved.description: `@nbparticules_rendu`: particles per source saved for display; 0 saves none.

random_seed.description:
`@random_seed`: 0 leaves the generator unseeded and runs one thread per band; any other
value seeds it and forces a single thread. The solver reads it as a C `int`.

receiver_radius_m.description: `@rayon_recepteurp`: point-receiver sphere radius, metres. Must be above 0.

sound_maps_per_band.description: `@output_recs_byfreq`: surface-receiver files for every band, not only the global one.

time_step_s.description: `@pasdetemps`, seconds. `duration / time step` must stay below 65,536 steps.

transmission.description: `@trans_calc`: transmission through materials that have a transmission loss.

SurfaceGroup.description: A named set of faces sharing one material: the unit materials are assigned to.

material.description: The base project's material; a [`Variant`] may override it.

oneOf.description:
On the model: every face of these surface groups carries this receiver's id as its `.cbin`
`idRs`. A face has one `idRs`, so a group belongs to at most one scene receiver.

A rectangle through corners `a`, `b`, `c` (`@ax`..`@cz`), cut into
`ceil(|bc| / resolution) x ceil(|ba| / resolution)` cells (`@resolution`, metres).

a.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

b.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

c.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

resolution_m.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

TcrSettings.description:
TCR, the classical theory of reverberation. TCR always writes surface receivers per band
(it tests the attribute's presence, not its value), so that switch is not a setting.

UpAxis.description: The vertical axis. Only +Z, as the solvers use it (`@alog`/`@blin` gradients act along z).

Variant.description: A named set of material overrides on top of the base project.

overrides.description: At most one per group, strictly ascending by group id (so each variant has one spelling).

ViewState.description: GUI state that belongs to the project.

camera.description: The saved 3D view; `None` lets the GUI frame the model.
